findings.issue: requestReturn takes the PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock on the order with orders.lockById(orderId) before find(userId, orderId) checks ownership. An authenticated user who knows another user's order UUID can therefore hold that order's row lock for the length of a transaction that ends in 404. The impact is negligible because UUIDs cannot be guessed and the lock is short.
findings.fix: Optionally check ownership first (find, then lock), or lock with an owner predicate such as lockByIdAndUserId.

findings.issue: AC-4 gap, already disclosed and on the backlog: the seller ledger books any part marked DELIVERED and does not treat CANCELLED as final. A forged or replayed DELIVERED for a cancelled shipment would book SALE, COMMISSION or FEE. order-service itself cannot advance a CANCELLED shipment, and events are keyed by orderId on one partition, so the only route is a forged or stale event.
findings.fix: Track the follow-up: before booking, seller-service should refuse DELIVERED for a shipment it has seen as CANCELLED.

summary: I reviewed PR-B (0727afe..b4c7f44) for over-refund between returns and cancels and for the seller ledger. I found no over-refund. completesOrder now counts only cancelled shipments (DONE) as covered, and shippingAlreadyRefunded also counts a cancel claim in REQUESTED or DONE that carries shipping. FAILED claims are left out of both, so shipping goes either to the completing cancel or to the completing return, never both. If a REQUESTED claim that held the shipping goes FAILED, it frees the shipping; when it is claimed again, cancelShare finds any return that has since taken the shipping and freezes 0. Return amounts stay pro rata (paidShare), and the cancel remainder subtracts every non-rejected return, so the total stays at paid items plus shipping once, give or take the existing per-return HALF_UP cents that payment-service caps anyway. The other mismatch I found is possible lost shipping when a return completes the order while a sibling cancel is still in flight. That is an under-refund, not an over-refund. requestReturn now locks the order row first, so the return-time shipping and completion decisions are serialised with cancel claims and commits. Seller ledger: OrderEventConsumer reverses only on RETURN_REFUNDED: through reverseReturn when the event has returnId and refundAmount, otherwise through reverseRefund when parts are marked refunded or the payment status is REFUNDED. SHIPMENT_STATUS_CHANGED and ORDER_CANCELLED for a cancel take neither path, and only the idempotent DELIVERED booking runs for parts that really are delivered. A cancelled shipment was never delivered, so nothing is booked and nothing needs reversing (CancelEventShapeTest pins the event shape). The runbook adds the persistent-decline manual path and the queries for stuck rows and FAILED claims whose sibling holds the shipping. The delta adds no new endpoint, input, secret or dependency. Minors: lock taken before the ownership check in requestReturn (negligible), and the disclosed AC-4 seller-ledger gap. My earlier backlog minors still stand: the PENDING settle watch, merging A together with B, and the seller's free-text reason in the customer timeline.
